label: conj:type-b-folding-cpt
title: Type-B Cartan folding realises CPT via symmetric-crystal $\mathbb{Z}/2$ fixed points
html:
Conjecture. Type-B Cartan folding realises CPT via symmetric-crystal \mathbb{Z}/2 fixed points

Conjecture (Type-B folding closure). The \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum on the canonical atomic-braid Hecke algebra H_n(q) folds into a Type-B Cartan datum \mathrm{B}_{n/2} under the involution \iota: \alpha_i \leftrightarrow \alpha_{n-i}. The resulting Kashiwara crystal is a symmetric crystal whose GS normal forms are bar-involution invariant by construction. Stable matter = fixed points of the folded crystal; antimatter = the \iota-orbit complement. Under this folding, the composite CPT operator decomposes naturally as a tensor of:

  • C from color-sheet flavor conjugation
  • P from Type-B Cartan folding
  • T from Markov-trace cyclicity

Type-B folding provides an alternative categorical realisation where the role of "P (braid mirror)" is replaced by "the Cartan-fold Z/2", and the bar-invariance emerges from the Type-B symmetric-crystal structure rather than from explicit \sigma_{i} \leftrightarrow \sigma_{i}^{-1} braid manipulation. The Type-B folding view is more compact but requires more category theory.
